problem: BeBee has no deterministic Defold unit-test runner or data-validation boundary, so production logic/content could regress without an editor-independent, machine-readable failure signal.

decision.rationale: Use a small repository-local Lua runner inside a dedicated Defold headless bootstrap, with the existing pinned Bob/Java contract and a dependency-free process controller. This follows current Defold automated-testing guidance while avoiding an unnecessary third-party framework.

research.candidate_pool_exception: Shipped-game competitor research is not applicable to a test/data infrastructure ticket; engine/runtime correctness is governed by Defold technical contracts.
research.reference_exception: No player-facing interaction or presentation decision is made.

anti_pattern.observation: A host-only test can miss engine-specific behavior and a CI process that only looks for any log output can falsely pass a crashed or incomplete suite.
anti_pattern.lesson: Run engine-dependent tests in a dedicated Defold bootstrap and require a structured completion event plus process exit status.

official_docs.verified_constraint: Defold documents dedicated test bootstraps, Bob headless bundles, captured exit status/logs, timeout enforcement and a required structured suite-completion event for CI.
Bob supports dedicated settings, x86_64-linux bundles and the headless engine variant used by the test process controller.
sys.exit(code) terminates the Defold application with an explicit process exit code that can propagate suite failure.

alternatives.reason: Runs in the real Defold Lua environment, stays dependency-free and exactly covers the small P0 test/data requirement.
A new dependency/license/version surface is not justified by the initial small suite; it can be revisited if the local runner becomes burdensome.
Host-only Lua/Python execution would not prove behavior in Defold's Lua environment and can miss engine globals such as hash().

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A dedicated non-production Defold test bootstrap executes deterministic Lua suites without changing the production bootstrap.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/test.settings overrides only main_collection to tests/test_bootstrap.collectionc; game.project remains unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The data validator rejects duplicate/malformed stable IDs and broken authored cross-references with deterministic diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: data/validator.lua implements sorted structural/reference errors and tests/test_data_validation.lua includes positive and adversarial cases.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The first deterministic suite covers merged production input semantics as well as the data-validation contract.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/test_input_semantics.lua and tests/test_data_validation.lua define eleven deterministic cases executed by tests/test_runner.script.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The editor-independent test command propagates build/test failure through process status and requires structured suite completion.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tools/defold/run_tests.py verifies pinned Bob/Java, builds the documented headless target, enforces a timeout, parses BEBEE_TEST JSON, requires one passing suite_end event and exit code 0.

automated: Repository standards validate Python/JSON/text hygiene and the explicit tests non-production root on the exact candidate source.

The stacked BB-004 CI wiring PR runs bash scripts/test.sh against the combined exact head before this harness is merged, providing the runtime execution proof without mixing runtime Lua and governance workflow changes in one PR.
verification.runtime_errors: The headless process controller retains the complete engine log and treats build errors, timeout, malformed/missing completion, failed cases or any non-zero exit as failure; exact runtime execution is bound to the stacked CI PR before merge.

known_limitations: The foundation validates catalog structure/references only; domain-specific flower/economy constraints are added with the content systems that own them.
CI workflow wiring is intentionally a separate process PR so the trusted base classification policy is not weakened or bypassed.
